global_guidance.product_procurement_strategy:
Product procurement is usually awarded based on Lowest Price Technically Acceptable. Agencies want the cheapest vendor who meets the specs. Margins can be slim, but here's the upside — one competitive supplier can fulfill contracts nationwide. Vendors are often ready to ship across the country, which means you can scale fast.

Many brokers overlook the volume game. One good product vendor can let you respond to ten or twenty solicitations every week. Use bid platforms, saved searches, and daily alerts to keep opportunities flowing.
global_guidance.service_contract_strategy:
Service contracts typically last three to five years. They’re great for recurring, passive income if you maintain the relationship. However, most service providers operate regionally. If you want to perform a contract in another state or region, you’ll need to source a new vendor.

Agencies also value past performance. If you’re brokering services like janitorial or security, start with smaller contracts or offer subcontracting. Build a track record with vendors you trust.
global_guidance.retention_and_renewals: The effort is worth it. Perform well on a service contract and many agencies will offer renewals or extensions. One strong vendor relationship can generate revenue for years.
global_guidance.vendor_diversification: Never rely on one vendor. If they raise prices or drop out, your entire bid strategy can collapse. Always keep a bench of backup suppliers and contractors ready.

industries.name: Professional & Administrative Services
industries.summary: This industry includes the behind-the-scenes expertise and operational support that keeps government agencies running. From staffing and HR to financial services, project management, technical writing, and help desk support, these services help agencies stay compliant, organized, and efficient. For brokers, it’s a flexible category with high demand across nearly every department — ideal for connecting specialized vendors or freelancers with consistent contract needs.
industries.detailed_description: Professional & Administrative Services encompass any service where "people power" is the deliverable. Federal agencies regularly outsource these to handle surges in hiring, expand specialized skills, or fill short-term gaps. Major customers include GSA, DoD program offices, VA hospitals, diplomatic missions, and large civilian agencies. Contracts range from large IDIQs to small Blanket Purchase Agreements for ad-hoc support.
industries.broker_guidance:
- Certify subcontractors' credentials - HR consultants need SHRM-CP/PHR, CPAs need active licenses, interpreters need ATA certification
- Watch Service Contract Act wage determinations - ensure labor rates comply with correct WD classifications
- Build past performance for Best Value awards - compile case studies for each sub-industry showing successful outcomes
- Verify small business certifications in SAM.gov for set-aside opportunities
- Screen subcontractors for security clearance capability - many positions require Public Trust or Secret clearance

industries.name: Product Supply & Procurement
industries.summary: This category encompasses the procurement of physical goods, including office equipment, medical supplies, tactical gear, and construction materials. These contracts are often large-volume, fast-moving, and ideal for brokers who understand logistics, compliance, and sourcing. Many products fall under GSA schedules or BPA contracts, but there are always opportunities in open-market buys and emergency procurement.
industries.detailed_description: Product Supply & Procurement covers tangible goods purchased through GSA Schedules, DLA contracts, VA eBuy, or agency-specific solicitations. From bulk office stationery to high-end servers and surgical instruments, these are typically awarded under LPTA vehicles. Major contract vehicles include GSA MAS Schedules, SEWP, and DLA Distribution IDIQs.
industries.broker_guidance:
- Ensure product certifications - PPE must be NIOSH-approved, medical devices need FDA 510(k) clearance, electronics require UL certification
- Confirm stocking and lead times - price competitiveness requires guaranteed immediate or near-term delivery
- Verify GSA Schedule compliance including Price Reduction Clause and current Commercial Sales Practice
- Check CAGE codes for DLA items and ensure vendor registration in Defense Logistics Information Service database
- Maintain list of small business prime contractors with active certifications for low-value orders under $25K

industries.name: Information Technology & Cybersecurity
industries.summary: This industry powers the digital backbone of government operations. It includes everything from building secure networks and managing cloud infrastructure to developing custom software and protecting sensitive data from cyber threats. Agencies rely on trusted vendors for both day-to-day tech support and long-term modernization projects. It’s a high-demand space with strong budgets and consistent contract flow, but often requires certifications, clearances, and a strong technical track record to compete.
industries.detailed_description: IT & Cybersecurity services are among the fastest-growing segments in federal contracting, driven by mandates like CMMC, zero-trust architecture, and cloud-first directives. Agencies procure everything from managed SIEM services to custom application development. Common vehicles include CIO-SP3, Alliant 2, NIH CIO-SP4, and agency-level IDIQs.
industries.broker_guidance:
- Confirm vendor's corporate facility clearance and individual engineer security clearances for cybersecurity roles
- Verify CMMC Level 2 for DoD CUI handling or FedRAMP authorization for cloud services - request current ATO letters
- Ensure software stack is TAA-compliant and check for ITAR/EAR export control violations
- Prepare for task order competition on GWAC vehicles - gather multiple qualified prime contractors
- Maintain updated SBA profile documents for small business IT set-asides including 8(a), SDVOSB, HUBZone certifications

industries.name: Construction, Engineering & Specialized Services
industries.summary: This industry covers the planning, building, and upgrading of government facilities and infrastructure. It includes everything from renovating courthouses and military barracks to laying roads, installing HVAC systems, and managing full-scale design-build projects. Agencies like the VA, DoD, GSA, and DOT regularly issue contracts in this space to maintain and expand federal properties. It's a large, competitive industry with high-dollar contracts and a strong need for compliance, bonding, and qualified subcontractors. As a broker, you’ll often work with trade specialists or GC firms that need help navigating federal paperwork and teaming.
industries.detailed_description: This category captures everything from erecting new federal buildings to renovating NOAA labs, performing roadwork on military bases, or designing new VA clinics. Major award vehicles include Army Corps MATOCs, NAVFAC IDIQs, Air Force Prime Vendor contracts, and GSA's 3P partnerships. Activities range from high-dollar design-build projects over $100M to smaller task orders under $2M.
industries.broker_guidance:
- Verify NAICS code exact matching - NAICS 236220 for commercial building, NAICS 237310 for highway construction
- Confirm bonding capacity with Surety A rating and three years audited financials for Performance and Payment Bonds
- Ensure architect/engineer firms hold valid AIA or NSPE certifications for Design-Build projects
- Validate state-specific trade licenses - HVAC, Master Electrician, Journeyman Plumber licenses vary by jurisdiction
- Address NEPA reviews and Section 106 historic preservation requirements - verify vendor EPA/EH compliance willingness

industries.name: Healthcare & Medical Services
industries.summary: This industry supports the delivery of medical care across government-run hospitals, clinics, military treatment facilities, and detention centers. It includes everything from providing healthcare workers and equipment to supporting infrastructure like mobile units, laundry, and telemedicine. Agencies such as the VA, DoD, BOP, HHS, and FEMA frequently issue contracts in this space. As a broker, you'll need to work with vendors who can meet clinical standards, deliver at scale, and often respond quickly in emergencies or ongoing care cycles.
industries.detailed_description: Healthcare & Medical Services cover everything from staffing temporary clinicians at VA hospitals to supplying specialized imaging equipment to DoD medical facilities. Vehicles include VA's VHA acquisition tools, DoD's CHCS agreements, NIH CIO-SP4 for health IT, and HHS Purchase Order systems. Patient care emphasis requires strict regulatory compliance including HIPAA, FDA, and JCAHO standards.
industries.broker_guidance:
- Verify HIPAA compliance with current Risk Assessment, signed Business Associate Agreements, and FIPS 140-2 encryption
- Ensure FDA 510(k) clearance for DME and surgical instruments, plus current FDA establishment registration
- Confirm medical staff hold valid state licenses, DEA numbers, VA badge eligibility, and specialty certifications
- Align vendor SINs with GSA Schedule 70 or 132-56 for healthcare IT and medical services purchases
- For veterinary services, confirm AAALAC accreditation and CCAC-approved laboratory animal care compliance

subindustries.name: Medical Staffing & Temporary Health Personnel
subindustries.description: Provides doctors, nurses, therapists, and specialists on a contract or temporary basis for VA hospitals, military clinics, and federal prisons.
subindustries.broker_guidance: Credentials, background checks, and state licensure are non-negotiable. Work with staffing firms that specialize in healthcare and are used to credentialing and onboarding within federal timelines. Outsourcing to foreign companies can be a great way to lower your bottom line, just make sure they have all the required certificates.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Healthcare & Medical Services/Sub-Industries/Medical Staffing & Temporary Health Personnel 20e97366fb9e81eca78edb667a77fe0b.md

subindustries.description: Includes long-term medical devices like wheelchairs, oxygen machines, CPAP devices, hospital beds, and mobility aids.
subindustries.broker_guidance: Target vendors that are already registered with the VA’s FSS or DAPA. Delivery and service warranties are often bundled, so look for vendors who offer white-glove setup or on-site repairs.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Healthcare & Medical Services/Sub-Industries/Durable Medical Equipment (DME) 20e97366fb9e8105a9aad885ea09a2a9.md

subindustries.description: Includes gloves, masks, syringes, disinfectants, bandages, and other disposable essentials used daily in federal healthcare settings.
subindustries.broker_guidance: Margins are low, but demand is constant. Work with vendors who can deliver in bulk and meet FDA or NIOSH standards. Best suited for brokers seeking recurring, high-volume deals.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Healthcare & Medical Services/Sub-Industries/Medical Supplies (PPE, Bandages, etc ) 20e97366fb9e8119b92fca98a866b974.md

subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Healthcare & Medical Services/Sub-Industries/Health IT & EHR Systems 20e97366fb9e81d8b5ebcad91c7d8ded.md

subindustries.name: Telemedicine Services
subindustries.description: Telemedicine contracts provide remote healthcare services to veterans, rural patients, or emergency response units using virtual platforms. These services are critical for agencies like the VA, Indian Health Service, and FEMA when in-person care is limited or impractical.
subindustries.broker_guidance: This space is growing fast, but many of the top vendors already have federal relationships or are part of large health systems. Your edge is finding smaller platforms or regional providers that are HIPAA-compliant but haven’t broken into federal yet. Look for agencies posting pilot programs or expansion projects, especially those tied to rural access or behavioral health. Your value comes from simplifying onboarding and connecting these newer providers with the right entry points.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Healthcare & Medical Services/Sub-Industries/Telemedicine Services 20e97366fb9e81d9b32ac88df32943cd.md

industries.name: Operations & Facilities Support
industries.summary: This industry covers the day-to-day services that keep federal buildings, military bases, and government facilities running smoothly. From janitorial work and landscaping to HVAC repairs, pest control, and elevator maintenance, it includes everything related to maintaining, cleaning, and operating government spaces. These contracts are often recurring, location-based, and ideal for brokers who can connect reliable vendors to consistent facility needs.
industries.detailed_description: Operations & Facilities Support cover day-to-day upkeep of federal buildings, installations, and campuses including custodial services, landscape management, pest mitigation, minor repairs, and infrastructure support. Many agencies bundle these into Base Operating Support or Integrated Facilities Management agreements. Contracts are typically LPTA with guaranteed performance levels and specific KPIs.
industries.broker_guidance:
- Match Service Contract Act wage determinations exactly - confirm staff categories align with WD classifications down to labor-hour level
- Verify state licenses - pest control operators need structural licenses, elevator contractors need state certification and ASME A17.1 compliance
- Ensure robust QA/QC programs with monthly scorecards and corrective action tracking for performance KPIs
- Prepare for bundled vs unbundled opportunities - larger bases combine all trades under one prime contractor
- Check EPA Section 608 certification for HVAC refrigerants and state electrician licenses for electrical work

subindustries.name: Janitorial & Cleaning Services
subindustries.description: Routine custodial services for federal offices, courthouses, VA hospitals, and military facilities. Includes daily cleaning, disinfection, and occasional deep cleans.
subindustries.broker_guidance:
👉 There's a ton of volume in this space but competition is usually high

Expect dozens of bids per solicitation, especially on SAM or GSA. Focus on brokering vendors with consistent staffing, strong past performance, and the ability to service multiple sites. Great niche for recurring revenue once a foothold is secured.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Operations & Facilities Support/Sub-Industries/Janitorial & Cleaning Services 20e97366fb9e81ceb056f8cecf742e1c.md

subindustries.name: Landscaping & Grounds Maintenance
subindustries.description: Lawn care, tree trimming, irrigation maintenance, and snow removal for federal campuses, cemeteries, and base perimeters.
subindustries.broker_guidance:
👉 Landscaping contracts are everywhere but they’re highly localized and competitive

Federal agencies award a high number of grounds maintenance contracts especially through the VA and GSA Most go to small businesses near the site so your edge as a broker comes from knowing which vendors are local reliable and ready to respond year-round including for snow and storm cleanup
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Operations & Facilities Support/Sub-Industries/Landscaping & Grounds Maintenance 20e97366fb9e81bdadbbc13207ee4006.md

subindustries.name: Pest Control
subindustries.description: Extermination and preventive pest management in office buildings, hospitals, military housing, and warehouses.
subindustries.broker_guidance:
👉 What makes this niche attractive is the lower competition and clear compliance standards — most solicitations require valid state pest control licenses, proof of technician training, and EPA-compliant products. That creates a barrier for less-prepared vendors, which is where a strong broker brings value.

Focus on vendors who:

- Already serve commercial or institutional clients (schools, hotels, or local gov)
- Are licensed in the contract’s target state
- Can provide MSDS sheets and safety plans up front
- Have experience with IPM (Integrated Pest Management), which many agencies now prefer
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Operations & Facilities Support/Sub-Industries/Pest Control 20e97366fb9e81719081cf00297743fb.md

subindustries.name: Laundry & Linen Services
subindustries.description: Includes linen cleaning for VA hospitals, correctional facilities, and temporary FEMA housing. Covers bedding, uniforms, scrubs, and towels.
subindustries.broker_guidance: 👉 Volume is key. V endors with commercial-scale capacity, fast turnaround, and experience with medical or correctional-grade sanitation do the best work and have the best prices. Your edge is connecting the gov to reliable bulk operators who can deliver consistently.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Operations & Facilities Support/Sub-Industries/Laundry & Linen Services 20e97366fb9e81fd9b13d8787e2ff01c.md

subindustries.name: Facilities Maintenance & Repair
subindustries.description: General upkeep of federal buildings including lighting, door repairs, plumbing fixes, and HVAC troubleshooting. Often part of integrated facilities management contracts.
subindustries.broker_guidance:
👉 This niche rewards brokers who can combine multiple trades into one offer
Agencies need a mix of services like lighting, doors, drywall, and plumbing. You’ll stand out by brokering a team of reliable handymen or maintenance pros under a bundled service model.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Operations & Facilities Support/Sub-Industries/Facilities Maintenance & Repair 20e97366fb9e8131a1e9ca18b9668b5a.md

subindustries.name: HVAC, Electrical, Plumbing, and Specialized Trades
subindustries.description: Covers licensed mechanical work such as HVAC tune-ups, panel replacements, re-wiring, and emergency plumbing response.
subindustries.broker_guidance:
👉 These trades require certified technicians and fast response times
Most contracts are tied to military bases, VA campuses, or leased GSA buildings. Brokers should focus on subs who are licensed, bonded, and can meet government safety protocols on short notice. Look for companies that service commercial clients, they usually have wholesale pricing, whereas residential companies don’t.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Operations & Facilities Support/Sub-Industries/HVAC, Electrical, Plumbing, and Specialized Trades 20e97366fb9e8184b5b2c5cfacac5356.md

subindustries.name: Elevator Maintenance
subindustries.description: Inspection, repair, and 24/7 emergency service of elevator systems in federal facilities, VA hospitals, and courthouses.
subindustries.broker_guidance: These contracts go to vendors with specific certifications and documented inspection records. If you can secure a partner that’s already servicing municipal or hospital elevators, this is a great long-term play. Otis and Schindler are big players in this game. They are open to teaming arrangements.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Operations & Facilities Support/Sub-Industries/Elevator Maintenance 20e97366fb9e81c382c3e60cb6e1de06.md

subindustries.name: Waste Management & Recycling
subindustries.description: Covers garbage collection, hazardous waste disposal, e-waste handling, and the implementation of recycling programs.
subindustries.broker_guidance:
👉 Things to Know as a Broker:

This niche is logistics-heavy with strict compliance. Most agencies want local vendors who can handle recurring pickups, provide disposal logs, and follow EPA or OSHA rules. Focus on matching regional haulers to federal sites nearby — proximity often wins.

Medical or hazardous waste requires extra licensing, so get ahead of that paperwork early. For general waste, pricing is usually by ton or per pickup. You can also bundle waste with janitorial or facility services to create more attractive offers. Green vendors get priority. If your vendor recycles or tracks landfill diversion, highlight that in your bid. It's a great selling point in technical evaluations.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Operations & Facilities Support/Sub-Industries/Waste Management & Recycling 20e97366fb9e81ebae48ed13c293f445.md

subindustries.name: Snow Removal & Outdoor Maintenance
subindustries.description: Seasonal contracts for plowing, salting, walkway clearing, and outdoor upkeep on military bases, VA facilities, and border installations.
subindustries.broker_guidance:
These contracts are highly seasonal and time-sensitive. Agencies issue them ahead of winter and expect fast, reliable service — often with guaranteed response times after snowfall. Brokers should work with vendors that have their own plows, salt trucks, and 24/7 crews on standby.
Many contracts are regional, covering multiple federal buildings in a city or county. Pricing is often structured per event, per inch of snow, or as a flat monthly rate for seasonal coverage.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Operations & Facilities Support/Sub-Industries/Snow Removal & Outdoor Maintenance 20e97366fb9e817398c7fd783c673cfb.md

industries.name: Logistics, Transportation & Supply Chain
industries.summary: This industry manages how goods, vehicles, and people move across the government ecosystem. From delivering disaster relief supplies to relocating military families, these services are essential to federal operations. Contracts range from bulk freight shipments and warehousing to last-mile deliveries and fleet maintenance. It’s a fast-moving space that rewards vendors with strong coordination, speed, and reliability. As a broker, you’ll be matching agencies with providers who can handle time-sensitive, high-volume, or specialized transport needs.
industries.detailed_description: Logistics, Transportation & Supply Chain services focus on moving people and goods whether shipping DLA-managed materiel to combat zones, staging relief convoys, or managing GSA fleet vehicles. The Department of Transportation, DLA, DoD, and FEMA are primary customers. Contracts include long-term IDIQ Requirements Contracts and ad-hoc Disaster Response BPAs.
industries.broker_guidance:
- Verify MilRun credentials and current DUNS plus CAGE code in Active status in SAM.gov with Active NCAGE
- Ensure DOT HM-126F training for hazardous materials handlers plus active HM license and carrier authorization
- Confirm USPPI documentation for overseas shipping and correct export licenses for ITAR/EAR-sensitive cargo
- Check GSA G-Fleet certification for auto-dealer partners offering maintenance at GSA Advantage pricing
- Verify 24/7 surge capacity with tiered network of carriers and warehouses across multiple regions for disaster relief

subindustries.name: Freight & Cargo Shipping
subindustries.description: Involves moving large shipments of goods, equipment, or materials between government locations by truck, rail, or container.
subindustries.broker_guidance: Federal freight often requires specialized logistics like secure handling or temperature control. Use vendors familiar with military or FEMA shipments
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Logistics, Transportation & Supply Chain/Sub-Industries/Freight & Cargo Shipping 20e97366fb9e8104b24cee8ddcbc7378.md

subindustries.name: Courier & Delivery Services
subindustries.description: Covers smaller, often time-sensitive deliveries between government offices or remote facilities.
subindustries.broker_guidance: These contracts favor vendors with tracking capabilities and flexible routes. USPS isn’t always used, so private couriers are in demand.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Logistics, Transportation & Supply Chain/Sub-Industries/Courier & Delivery Services 20e97366fb9e81578f01e717fe1d683e.md

subindustries.broker_guidance: Match agencies with vendors who can support large fleets and offer telematics or preventative maintenance programs.

industries.name: Research & Development
industries.summary: This industry supports the government’s pursuit of innovation, scientific advancement, and operational efficiency. Contracts span across defense, health, tech, and energy — often awarded to universities, private labs, or cutting-edge startups. Many opportunities are tied to SBIR/STTR programs, pilot programs, or large-scale innovation grants. Brokers who understand how to package niche technical capabilities or connect non-traditional vendors can unlock long-term, high-value partnerships.
industries.detailed_description: Research & Development contracts fund basic science, applied research, and prototype demonstrations. Agencies include DoD (DARPA, ONR, Army Research Lab), DOE national labs, NASA, NIH, and NSF. Vehicles include SBIR/STTR awards, Broad Agency Announcements, and large multi-agency R&D IDIQs. Competition is lower than average but technical rigor is extremely high.
industries.broker_guidance:
- Verify SBIR/STTR eligibility - firms must be US-owned, for-profit, under 500 employees with valid SBA SAM profile
- Assemble university partners and subject matter experts to craft compelling 5-page technical whitepapers
- Understand IP and data rights distinctions - guide clients on Government Purpose License vs Unlimited Rights
- Ensure valid IRB or IACUC protocols for human or animal subjects research with proper institutional approvals
- Coordinate NDAA or CRADA teaming arrangements in advance for multi-site consortium proposals

subindustries.name: Scientific Research Services
subindustries.description: Includes laboratory research, environmental studies, biomedical research, and defense-related science.
subindustries.broker_guidance: Universities dominate here, but boutique labs and private researchers often go overlooked. Look for niche expertise and help navigate grant-backed solicitations.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Research & Development/Sub-Industries/Scientific Research Services 20e97366fb9e817fa7f8d2059a4dfde0.md

subindustries.name: Product Development (Tech, Health, Military)
subindustries.description: Developing specialized tools, software, devices, or hardware for government use.
subindustries.broker_guidance: Great space for startups and innovation firms. Your value is helping them enter GovCon via pilot programs or sub-award teaming.
subindustries.source_file: WAR DOGS ACADEMY/Industries/Research & Development/Sub-Industries/Product Development (Tech, Health, Military) 20e97366fb9e81f0b1ffc6c34d9369e5.md

subindustries.name: Prototype Testing & Evaluation
subindustries.description: Testing new products, vehicles, weapons systems, or software for functionality, compliance, and deployment readiness.
